extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent applicants/agents (practitioners) involved in prosecution before the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedures governing shortened statutory periods, specified time limits, and extensions of time (37 CFR 1.136) for replies to Office actions, including consequences of failure to reply, calculation of deadlines, and special situations (final rejection, Notice of Allowability, affidavits, holidays).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum shortened statutory period
rubrics_metrics.description: A shortened statutory period may not be less than 30 days (35 U.S.C. 133).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use at least 30 days when setting a shortened statutory period for reply. (See MPEP § 710.02(c).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations warranting 1‑month shortened statutory period
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reply by an applicant for a nonfinal Office action is bona fide but includes an inadvertent omission, the examiner may set a 1 month (not less than 30 days) shortened statutory time period to correct the omission. (Also: requirement for restriction or election of species only — see MPEP § 809.02(a) and § 817.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply a 1‑month shortened period for limited formal corrections or inadvertent omissions; cite appropriate MPEP sections when setting such periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations warranting 2‑month shortened statutory period
rubrics_metrics.description: A 2‑month shortened statutory period should be set for certain situations, e.g., winning party in a terminated interference to reply to an unanswered Office action (MPEP § 2363.02), to reply to an Ex parte Quayle Office action when application is otherwise in condition for allowance but for formal matters (MPEP § 714.14), and multiplicity rejection — no other rejection (MPEP § 2173.05(n)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When application is special or prompt action is required to correct formal matters (Quayle), or in other listed situations, set a 2‑month shortened period and indicate prosecution on the merits is closed where appropriate (PTOL‑326 notation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations warranting 3‑month shortened statutory period
rubrics_metrics.description: To reply to any Office action on the merits, a 3‑month shortened statutory period is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default shortened statutory period for merits Office actions is three months unless another period is specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specified time limits (non‑statutory) and their consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain actions may be given a specified time (often <30 days) which is not a shortened statutory period under 35 U.S.C. 133, and failure to timely take the specific action results in a consequence other than abandonment of the entire application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (A) Petition under 37 CFR 1.14(e) for public access — applicant usually given ~3 weeks to state objections; failure to reply results in decision on petition without applicant's objections (MPEP § 103). (B) IDS that omits part of 37 CFR 1.98 content — examiner may set 1‑month time to complete IDS; failure results in noncompliant material placed in file but not considered (MPEP § 609). (C) When application is allowable but contains traverse of a restriction requirement — applicant may be given 1 month to cancel non‑elected claims; failure treated as authorization to cancel and application passed to issue (37 CFR 1.141 and 1.144; MPEP § 809.02(c), § 821.01). (Suggested claims for interference must be presented within not less than one month; failure treated as disclaimer — see MPEP § 2305.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between specified time limits and shortened statutory periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Specified time limits and shortened statutory periods have different penalties and procedural consequences: failure to meet a specified time affects rights in a particular matter, while failure to reply within a shortened statutory period under 35 U.S.C. 133 results in abandonment of the entire application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abandonment under 35 U.S.C. 133 is not appealable; revival may be possible under 37 CFR 1.137(a) (unavoidable) or 1.137(b) (unintentional). Specified times may be set for less than 30 days and may be excused by the examiner if a short delay is satisfactorily explained, whereas a late reply to a shortened statutory period (even by 1–2 days) results in abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) — petition and fee procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If required to reply within a nonstatutory or shortened statutory time period, applicant may extend the time up to the earlier of the expiration of any maximum period set by statute or five months after the time period set for reply, by filing a petition for an extension of time and the fee set in § 1.17(a), unless exceptions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key points: (1) Filing date of petition and fee determines extension period and fee amount; (2) reply must be filed prior to expiration of the period of extension to avoid abandonment (§ 1.135); (3) petition and fee may be filed prior to, with, or without the reply; (4) extensions under 1.136(a) are effective on filing/payment without Office acknowledgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive petitions under 37 CFR 1.136(a)(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: A written request in an application authorizing treatment of any concurrent or future reply requiring a petition under 1.136(a) as incorporating a petition for extension, an authorization to charge all required fees to a deposit account, or submission of the fee in § 1.17(a) will be treated as a constructive petition for an extension of time in any concurrent or future reply requiring a petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision serves as a 'safety net' when applicants omit an explicit petition. The Office nevertheless strongly recommends including a written petition in the reply to avoid processing delays. Examples and practice: an authorization or prior written request/fee submission can make later petitions effective; Office practice may construe petitions to request sufficient extension to make the filing timely if fee authorization exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.136(b) extensions — sufficient cause and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: When 1.136(a) is not available, the period for reply may be extended under 1.136(b) only for sufficient cause and for a reasonable time specified; any request must be filed on or before the day the reply is due and must state a reason in support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mere filing of a request under (b) does not effect an extension. Extensions under (b) are decided by the Technology Center Director. No extension may extend reply beyond any statutory maximum (e.g., 6 months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions where extensions are not available
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136 are not available in certain circumstances: (A) reexamination proceedings (37 CFR 1.550(c)); (B) during interference proceedings (except preparatory to an interference where a claim is suggested for interference); (C) when an Office action states 1.136(a) is not applicable (e.g., reply to a notice of allowability, litigation‑related reissue applications, or application in allowable condition with nonelected claims and time set to cancel such claims); and (D) limited instances where applicant is given a specified time limit to take actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept extension petitions in these excluded contexts; cite the appropriate CFR/MPEP provision when denying or explaining non‑availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for extensions — cumulative fees and small entity discount
rubrics_metrics.description: The fees for extensions of time are set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(a) and are cumulative; small entities qualify for a 50% reduction. If successive month extensions are taken, compute the proper fee as the difference between cumulative tiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: If applicant already paid 1‑month fee (tier 1) and later needs an additional month, the proper fee is the tier‑2 amount minus the tier‑1 amount previously paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing/acceptance of late reply when petition/fee missing or insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a reply is filed after the set period and no petition/fee accompanies it, the reply will not be accepted as timely until the petition (which may be constructive under 1.136(a)(3)) and the appropriate fee are submitted. If the petition filed requests an insufficient extension, additional fees corresponding to the further extension are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Office action sets a 3‑month shortened period, applicant replies in the 4th month and files only a 1‑month petition; reply is not acceptable until the fee is filed; if fee filed in 5th month, additional fee for second month extension will be required to render reply timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental replies where first reply was timely
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension of time under 37 CFR 1.136 is not necessary when submitting a supplemental reply to an Office action if a complete first reply was timely filed in reply to the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A supplemental paper can be filed without an extension provided the initial full reply was timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final rejection — required shortened period language and advisory‑action calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each final rejection must include specified language informing applicant that a shortened statutory period for reply is set to expire three months from the date of the action and explaining the special rule: if a first reply is filed within two months and the examiner's advisory action is not mailed until after the end of the three months, then the shortened statutory period will expire on the date the advisory action is mailed; in no event will the period extend beyond six months from the date of the final action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the exact required paragraph in each final rejection. Use advisory action mailing date for computing extension fees when the applicant filed a first reply within two months and the advisory action was mailed after the three‑month period. See MPEP § 710.02(e) for full mandatory wording and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions to submit affidavits after final rejection — discretionary and may not save application
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for extension of time to submit affidavits after final rejection may be granted to avoid abandonment, but the examiner may question why the affidavit was not earlier presented and may deny entry of the affidavit if the showing is insufficient; admission or refusal of the affidavit does not necessarily save the application from abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat affidavits submitted after final rejection as amendments after final rejection; the grant of an extension merely keeps the application from becoming abandoned to allow presentation of the affidavit, but entry is subject to 37 CFR 1.113 and examiner discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: No extensions after payment of issue fee / Notice of Allowability limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory nonextendable time period for payment of the issue fee is three months from the date of the Notice of Allowance (35 U.S.C. 151). Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) or (b) are NOT available to correct informalities identified on the Notice of Allowability; such informalities must be corrected and issue fee paid within the three‑month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If informalities (e.g., drawing corrections, supplemental declarations) are outstanding at allowance, notify applicant on PTOL‑37 and require correction within the nonextendable 3‑month period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two different periods running — how to determine controlling date
rubrics_metrics.description: When two different periods for reply are running (one regular statutory period from an earlier unanswered rejection and another limited period set in a subsequent Office action), the running of the first period is not suspended by an ex parte limited time action. In cases where claims are copied from a patent and rejected, the date of the last unanswered Office action on the claims other than the copied patent claims is the controlling date of the statutory period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume a later limited time action suspends earlier statutory periods; compute control dates per MPEP examples (see Ex parte Milton).

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of due date when extension granted — use date stamped/printed on action
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request for extension is granted, the due date is computed from the date stamped or printed on the action (i.e., the Office action’s date as printed/stamped when the extension is granted), not from the original due date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: OA dated November 30 with a 3‑month shortened period is due February 28; if extended one month, due date becomes March 30 (not March 28). See MPEP § 710.02(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Weekend/holiday rule for deadlines (35 U.S.C. 21 and 37 CFR 1.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the last day for taking any action or paying a fee falls on Saturday, Sunday, or a Federal holiday within the District of Columbia, the action may be taken, or the fee paid, on the next succeeding business day which is not a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday. For provisional application 12‑month periods, if the 12‑month day falls on a weekend/holiday, pendency extended to next business day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply this rule to all specified time periods/counting calendar days. See list of Federal holidays in MPEP and 5 U.S.C. 6103 for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of 37 CFR 1.136(b) duplicate requests and notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request under 1.136(b) is filed in duplicate with a stamped return‑address envelope, the Office will indicate action taken on the duplicate and return it promptly; notation on original (file record) should be signed and the duplicate returned should also show action taken and signer’s name/title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If duplicate not provided, applicant should be advised promptly of action taken so file record is complete. When granted/denied/in part, indicate the result on original and returned copy or send a formal decision letter. Use Form paragraphs 7.98 / 7.98.01 where reply is late but extension possible.
